name: Papua New Guinea
summary_text: Papua New Guinea is dangerous for trans visitors. Male same-sex conduct is criminalised (up to 14 years), and PNG has extreme levels of gender-based violence generally — among the world's highest documented rates. Port Moresby and Lae are dangerous cities for everyone; tribal-justice dynamics and police brutality affect marginalised people severely. There is no legal gender recognition, no LGBT organisation operating openly at national level, and sorcery-accusation violence shares the same social mechanics as anti-trans violence. For a visitor: the trans-specific risk is inseparable from the general security situation, which is among the worst in the Pacific.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA World Database jurisdiction page for Papua New Guinea: documents the legal status of same-sex conduct (criminalised under colonial-era law, up to 14 years) and gender-recognition data.
ADB publication on the legal status of sexual and gender minorities in Asia and the Pacific - regional comparative overview including Papua New Guinea.

sources.title: Where Violence Against Women is Rampant | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (Jan 2009): 'Where Violence Against Women is Rampant' - documents widespread gender-based violence in Papua New Guinea, the context of impunity that also affects sexual and gender minorities.

sources.title: Papua New Guinea's gay and transgender community finds safety in Hanuabada village - ABC News
sources.claim_summary: ABC News (Oct 2014): 'Papua New Guinea's gay and transgender community finds safety in Hanuabada village' - the coastal village on Port Moresby's outskirts (best known for producing half the national cricket team) is a safe haven for the gay and trans community in a country where homosexuality is illegal.

sources.title: Human Rights Watch says Papua New Guinea has failed to protect women and children | Human rights | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (Jan 2017): HRW says PNG has failed to respond to corruption and police violence and failed to protect women and children - a scathing assessment including Australia's offshore detention on the island.

sources.title: Papua New Guinea Has A Village For LGBT Community | The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News
sources.claim_summary: Guardian (Nigeria) Life (Nov 2018): 'Papua New Guinea Has A Village For LGBT Community' - openly gay 24-year-old Kapera Patrick remembers thugs pelting him with abuse, stones and bottles; Hanuabada village offers refuge where gay sex is illegal and stigma and violence are widespread.
